policy.claim: No external catalogue can guarantee a single 100% pronunciation for every Arabic name/term because connected speech, case endings, dialect/allophony and brand readings can differ.
hierarchy: brand-owner-approved override for exact DĀR AL TAWḤĪD product/brand strings
Qurʾānic phonetic/transcription reference where relevant to lexical forms
scientific romanization standard for spelling/transliteration only
pedagogical sources only as secondary confirmation
policy.lexicalVerification: Prefer two independent confirmations for high-priority terms when possible; owner-recorded pronunciations are required for brand-specific readings.

sources.title: International Phonetic Alphabet / official IPA chart
notFor: word-level Arabic lexical pronunciation by itself
sources.licenseNote: Official IPA chart is published by the International Phonetic Association; do not copy chart layout/audio into product assets without following its stated licence.

sources.title: Arabic — Illustration of the IPA
sources.publisher: Journal of the International Phonetic Association / Cambridge University Press

sources.title: Quranic Arabic Corpus — Phonetic Transcription
sources.basis: Arabic Through the Quran, Alan Jones, Islamic Texts Society, 2008
sources.caveat: Used for linguistic/transcription verification only. Qurʾān recitation remains real-recording-only.

sources.title: ALA-LC Romanization Table — Arabic
sources.publisher: Library of Congress / American Library Association

sources.title: Arabic definite article — sun and moon letters
use: secondary pedagogical confirmation of al- assimilation before sun letters
sources.caveat: Secondary pedagogical source; primary phonetic authority remains JIPA/IPA.

sources.title: Arabic Speech Recognition Pronunciation Dictionary
sources.publisher: Linguistic Data Consortium / Qatar Computing Research Institute
sources.scale: ~2,000,000 pronunciation entries for ~526,000 Standard Arabic words
sources.caveat: LDC licence required; data must not be copied into this repository without the appropriate licence.

sources.title: ipa-dict — Arabic (Modern Standard) pronunciation dictionary
sources.provenance: Arabic IPA generated from Tim Buckwalter's Arabic Morphological Analyzer with UTF-8/IPA adaptations.
sources.license: MIT repository; verify any third-party provenance notices before vendoring derived subsets.
sources.caveat: Algorithmically generated; never overrides owner-recorded brand readings or higher-tier linguistic evidence by itself.

sources.title: orthography2ipa — Modern Standard Arabic research specification
sources.caveat: Project labels Arabic as research quality, not production/native-speaker gold; use only as corroboration.

sources.title: Modern Standard Arabic lexical stress — weight-sensitive description
sources.publisher: Cambridge University Press / Studies in Second Language Acquisition
sources.summary: MSA stress is predictable and weight-sensitive; final superheavy syllables attract stress, otherwise the rightmost heavy syllable is preferred subject to the language's stress domain.
